analysis.title: Iron Mountain Inc. (IRM): Investor group meeting with CFO and Head of Data Centers and ALM reinforces our positive growth outlook
key_insights: Reiterate Buy on IRM with a 12-month price target of $136 (25.0% upside from $108.78). The note follows an investor group meeting with CFO Barry Hytinen, Head of Data Centers and ALM Mark Kidd, and Head of IR Mark Rupe.

Data center signed backlog approaches $1.8bn of annualized revenue at full development, against about $1bn of current annual data center revenue. About 650 MW is tracking to energize over several years, roughly half within 18-24 months, versus about 540 MW operating now.
Backlog and unleased capacity give visibility into at least 20% data center revenue growth in 2027. Commencement schedules cover Northern Virginia, London, Amsterdam and Chicago.

About two-thirds of near-term capacity is in Richmond, where power and entitlements are secured. Rising new lease pricing, renewal spreads above 10% and operating leverage could lift data center EBITDA margins from the mid-50% range toward 60% over several years.

India development yields are at least 200-300 bps above IRM's typical 10-12% range, helped by lower labor and construction costs. IRM acquired the remaining interest in its Web Werks joint venture and has secured power in Mumbai and other markets.

The proposed 12-month data center development moratorium in Loudoun County would not affect IRM. IRM does not operate there and has permits for its fully leased Manassas campus in Prince William County. IRM has no undeveloped land in Texas, Georgia or Ohio.

Enterprise ALM revenue grew more than 50% y/y organically in 3Q, with penetration in the low-single-digit percent range across 240,000 clients. About 40% of Fortune 1000 accounts are under contract or receive services. Programs already won support the outlook for >25% organic ALM growth in 2027.
The ALM outlook assumes flat memory prices, so higher prices would add revenue upside. Gross profit benefit would be smaller because IRM's share of resale proceeds is set upfront with customers.

IRM expects its US Treasury processing contract to produce about $100mn of revenue in 2027 and more than $150mn if all contemplated volumes go to IRM at the historical form mix. Treasury revenue is expected at $40-45mn in 2026.

Four vendors won Treasury awards, but two appear to be doing little or no work and another is reportedly approved for limited schedules. IRM has FedRAMP High authorization and expanded processing capacity. The Treasury's estimated $600-700mn of manual labor cost has widened IRM's government pipeline.

RIM should see slightly positive organic storage volume growth and mid-single-digit RIM revenue growth, driven mainly by value-based pricing. Organic storage revenue grew more than 7% y/y in 3Q excluding the prior-year data management benefit, the strongest in over two years.
IRM sets pricing from client-level and ZIP-code-level inbound activity across about 1,400 facilities, not mechanically from inflation. Average record retention is about 15 years.

The $136 target uses 19.0x NTM + 1YR EPS of $7.16, a discount to the 20.2x median for self-storage and industrial REIT peers. The discount reflects execution risk in the shift from records management to data and technology.
GS estimates 2026E revenue of $7,996mn (+15.9%), EBITDA of $2,963mn and EPS of $2.52. For 2027E it estimates revenue of $8,764mn, EBITDA of $3,258mn and EPS of $2.77.
Leverage is high and free cash flow is negative. GS estimates net debt/EBITDA of 6.1x for 2026E, FCF of -$489mn in 2026E, and FCF turning positive at $85mn in 2028E. Capex is about $2.2bn a year.
The stock is down 10.9% over 3 months and 11.9% over 6 months, but up 25.5% over 12 months. GS cut the target from $155 on 6 Oct 2026 to $136 on 5 Nov 2026.

market_movers.rationale: Data center backlog, ALM growth and the Treasury digital solutions contract support growth, and durable RIM growth adds to it. The target implies 25.0% upside.

earnings_insights: IRM 3Q26 (reported): enterprise ALM revenue grew more than 50% y/y organically.
IRM 3Q26 (reported): organic storage revenue grew more than 7% y/y excluding the prior-year data management benefit, the strongest in more than two years.
GS estimates (not reported) for 4Q26E: adjusted EPS $0.69, revenue $2,040mn, adjusted EBITDA $780mn.
GS estimates (not reported) for FY2026E adjusted EPS of $2.52 (+21.6% y/y) and FY2027E of $2.77 (+9.9%). FY2025 adjusted EPS was $2.07 (reported).
GS estimates (not reported) for 1Q27E adjusted EPS of $0.55, 2Q27E of $0.72 and 3Q27E of $0.72.

trade_ideas.rationale: Growth across data centers, ALM and digital solutions, tied to AI demand and cross-selling, plus durable RIM growth, should drive valuation upside.
trade_ideas.risk: Competing technologies in records management, acquisition integration risk, financial leverage and FX risk.

risk_factors: Financial leverage, with net debt/EBITDA of 6.3x in 2025 and 6.1x in 2026E
Execution risk and medium-term financial uncertainty in the shift from legacy records management to a data and technology company
Digitization could cause destructions to exceed inbound volumes within customer cohorts
geopolitical: The proposed 12-month data center development moratorium in Loudoun County, Virginia would not affect IRM.
Possible post-election policy changes in Texas, Georgia and Ohio data center markets. IRM has no undeveloped land there.
